A report in Israeli media has revealed details of a secret global campaign to boycott Qatar launched just days after the Hamas attacks on October 7, 2023.
The newspaper Haaretz says one of Israel's most senior political advisers was behind the initiative. 
It says a group of 30 strategic consultants, campaigners, advertising professionals and government figures joined a WhatsApp group called to mount an international campaign against Qatar.
Those involved believed that they could force Hamas to release hostages taken into Gaza by doing so.
The campaign aimed to highlight what it alleged were Qatar's financial links with Hamas officials.
A website in several languages, social media accounts, and promotional materials were launched.
But the campaign was abruptly stopped a month after its launch, with no explanation.

Rami Khouri is Distinguished Fellow at American University of Beirut. He says were several reasons why Israel's campaign against Qatar didn't work.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Nepal is still assessing the scale of destruction caused by last month's flash floods, which swept away entire towns and villages near the border with China's autonomous region of Tibet. 
At least 1,350 people have been confirmed dead and another 5,000 are missing and presumed buried under the mud. 
In the worst-hit Rasuwa district, former MP Dawa Finjo survived only because he had returned to his ancestral home for a funeral and was away from Syapru Besi when the flood struck. 
He lost his son, daughter-in-law and grandchildren, while about 40 relatives across both sides of his family are also missing or dead. 
Much of Syapru Besi, a town popular with trekkers and tourists, has been washed away, leaving only a few structures standing on higher ground. 
Finjo says rebuilding the devastated valley could take 15 to 20 years, highlighting the enormous challenge facing communities still recovering from the disaster. 

Al Jazeera's Tony Cheng reports from Rasuwa district, Nepal.

Subscribe
title: Nepal floods: Former MP loses 40 family members in Rasuwa disaster
